comments.author: Aadi_880
comments.body:
If it looks like AI, it's going to get some hate. If it doesn't most people won't even care. That's the level of commitment people have. And even then, usually, good games gets passed regardless.

3D ai games receive more positive reception than 2D ones though.

And you should probably give the GenAI tag, even though nothing really happens if you don't.

comments.author: WubsGames
comments.body:
AI use is highly frowned at in the gaming industry,  mostly among players, and artists.  
  
Releasing a game on steam requires you to disclose any AI use, and it will 100% for sure be met with bad reviews comment, or discussions against the use of AI on you game. 

That is a bad thing on the surface, but you can also use it to drive traffic if you are careful.  
  
My advice is to limit AI use, be honest about places you did use AI, and then try to use any resulting the negative press to drive traffic towards your game or store page.

comments.author: Resres2208
comments.body:
It depends. If you game is fully vibe coded, many people (iNcluding myself) are genuinely not interested. It elicits the same feelings as a game that's just store assets. It also sounds "buggy", "generic" and "low effort". I generally discourage vibe coding at all, however won't hold it against someone for using AI to assist coding...


Game assets on the other hand I think people are much more forgiving of, unless you really put it right in their face with an AI capsule and AI textures everywhere you look. Whether or not you put a lot of work in, AI usage can make it seem like you haven't.

replies.author: Other-Football72
replies.body: You must be a coder. My experience is the opposite; people seem to care less about using AI to code, but the art is where they lose their shit.

replies.author: GentlemanModan
replies.body:
I completely agree. To be honest nobody cares about a cider if it's working. I imagine a lot of games have horrible code written by humans, but if it works and doesn't really impact experience nobody cares. I have seen simple indie games that had much higher system requirements that they should, maybe because of the backend. 

But at the end of the day "much higher" for indie games still means most of the modern computers don't care at all.

replies.author: Resres2208
replies.body:
I will admit that my experience coding will certainly make me somewhat biased. But you do make a good point. I can think of plenty of fun games that, were you to tell me they were vibe coded, i would still like.


I still do think that there is a "buggy" and "low effort" stigma around vibe coded games and I don't think it's just me who feels that way. I do feel a lot of vibe coded games are "hey look what I'm releasing after just 6 months", which doesn't usually produce something very high effort. But perhaps because vibe coding is relatively new, it is somewhat impossible for someone to have vibe coded a game for a long period of time...

comments.author: lyeeedar
comments.body:
My game is doing really well despite using AI. The key thing is for it to not LOOK like ai. So use local ai and Loras to modify the style until it looks unique.

And at the end of the day, make a good game. If your game feels low effort then there will be no positive reviews to balance the anti-ai negatives.

>The key thing is for it to not LOOK like ai. 

But it does? Especially the backgrounds.

Love how you said AI was used in "some art and music". How much is "some"?

replies.author: lyeeedar
replies.body:
>But it does? Especially the backgrounds.

In my opinion the difference is not in artefacting (as you can see from the backgrounds) but in art style. Most models have a base art style they produce, and that is what makes it seem 'ai' to me. Twist that to a different style, and it's fine. E.g. for mine, we constantly have people coming on the discord then surprised it's ai.

>Love how you said AI was used in "some art and music". How much is "some"?

Most. Some are hand drawn (e.g. uis), and some are ai base then hand edited afterwards, and some are full ai.

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body: Are the backgrounds AI? Because I see some telltale signs, such as the sometimes "chaotic" patterns. E.g, in the recurring wood paneling in #4 or the different styles of the japanese buildings in #11 (floors look very different from each other). The characters too have the "AI-look" I have seen shared by many other manga-inspired games, or at least how AI seems to imagine manga to look like.
